Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: The UK has left the EU and as a result, the trading transition period ended at 11 p.m. on 31 December 2020.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: You should continue to publish your contract notices via Public Contract Notices. However, there will be some changes on how your contract notice will be advertised and whether you use an ESPD or an SPD as follows:
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: If your Framework Agreement contract notice or PIN (if used as a call for competition) was published on PCS before 11 p.m. on 31 December 2020:
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Your contract notice will have been published throughout the UK via OJEU
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Suppliers (and subcontractors, where appropriate) will have been asked to complete an ESPD
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Any future call offs/notices/awards under this Framework Agreement will continue to be made via OJEU (as these will be linked to the original Framework Agreement contract notice raised in PCS)
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Any future call offs will require an ESPD to be completed by suppliers (and subcontractors, where appropriate)
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: If your Framework Agreement. Contract Notice or PIN (if used as a call for competition) was published on PCS at or after 11 p.m. on 31 December 2020:
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Your contract notice will be published via the Find a Tender Service (FTS) throughout the UK. This will happen automatically and you should therefore raise your contract notice in PCS as normal.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Suppliers (and subcontractors, where appropriate) need to complete an SPD
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Any Framework Agreement future call offs/notices/awards will continue to be made via FTS (as these will be automatically linked to the original DPS contract notice raised)
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: More information can be found in EU Exit and SPPN 11/2020
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: The following information has been produced to assist buyers when considering whether they should call-off from or set up a framework agreement.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: Once a requirement has been identified for goods or services, as part of developing your procurement sourcing strategy, you should consider if there are any existing arrangements which could meet your needs. Local procurement departments and Centres of Expertise will be able to assist in this process.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: If there are no existing arrangements, or if the sourcing strategy demonstrates that best value for money would be delivered by a direct award, you will have to determine whether awarding a contract or framework agreement would be more appropriate.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements

When Setting up a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: Once the framework agreement has been established the terms of the agreement should include instructions on how call-off contracts should be awarded. Your organisation may also produce further guidance for the identified users of the framework agreement on how a call-off contract should be undertaken.

content_blocks.text: When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: Was your Organisation expressly identified in the contract notice for the Framework Agreement you are looking to use?
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: Is there more than one framework agreement which could meet the need?
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: What are the terms laid down in the framework agreement for call-off contracts?
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: When calling off from a framework agreement, it is important to note that there is no scope to apply selection criteria . Selection criteria will have been applied when establishing the framework agreement and must not be repeated at the call-off stage.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: When an aspect of contract delivery has not been included in the framework agreement, but is relevant to the nature of the call-off contract, organisations should consider how best to address this in the call-off contract. Organisations should consider whether the terms laid down in the framework enable additional criteria. For example, where Fair Work practices have not been included in the framework agreement but there is an award criterion to tackle “sustainability”, it is possible to include more precise criteria under this broader heading to address Fair Work practices.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: Mini-competitions must generally be based on the same terms as those which were applied for the award of the framework. However, The Public Contract (Scotland) Regulations 2015 allows that where necessary criteria for mini-competitions:
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: may be more precisely formulated
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: that other terms referred to in the procurement documents for the framework, may be applied where appropriate.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: For further considerations and an example of a typical mini-competition process consult the Guide for the use of Framework Agreements.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: Detailed guidance for conducting a mini-competition should be available from the owner of the framework agreement. However there are specific rules which are applicable to all mini-competitions.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: The call off must be placed with the supplier who has submitted the most economically advantageous, on the basis of the award criteria set out in the framework agreement. Unsuccessful tenderers must be notified of the outcome when a contract is awarded under a framework agreement.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
When Calling Off from a Framework Agreement

content_blocks.text: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

content_blocks.text: Organisations must ensure that current and future framework agreements (including those entered into before the legislation came into force) are compliant with GDPR. All relevant procurement documents must make reference to the relevant legislation.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

content_blocks.text: When using framework agreements, and if required, organisations should review each call-off to ensure all relevant procurement documents have been updated to reflect the new legislation.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

content_blocks.text: More detailed information on GDPR can be found in Additional Resources .
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

content_blocks.text: You may choose to follow the standstill rules on a voluntary basis when awarding an above-threshold contract by mini-competition in order to mitigate against an ineffectiveness order resulting from a legal challenge.
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

content_blocks.text: Speculative Framework Agreements
heading_path: Impact of EU Exit on Framework Agreements
Speculative Framework Agreements

content_blocks.text: It is recommended that you treat claims that speculative framework agreements offer the prospect of “full procurement law compliance” with caution, please refer to SPPN 3/2017 for further information.
